stage_profile_57600.interpretation: Statistics pass is the largest Triton component; metadata is negligible.

bottlenecks: Dense SDPA is 5.97x faster than the current Triton sparse path at 57,600 tokens.
The two-pass Triton design pays QK twice: output online-softmax plus statistics recomputation.
Statistics kernel is about 1.74x the output kernel cost per 240-token chunk at 57,600 tokens.
Sparse output quality error versus dense is large (relative L2 about 0.745), reflecting selected-route approximation rather than Triton numerics.
Triton and PyTorch sparse outputs agree closely (relative L2 about 0.0064), so the kernel is numerically consistent.
advantages: Triton directional is 2.08x faster than PyTorch directional at 57,600 tokens.
Triton statistics match PyTorch statistics within about 0.06% mass error and about 1.4% centroid error.
Route metadata construction is no longer a meaningful bottleneck.
limitations: Still substantially slower than dense SDPA because dense cuDNN/Flash kernels are much better optimized.
Second QK pass doubles compute and memory traffic for directional statistics.
Synthetic quality uses random Q/K/V, so relative error is an upper-bound-style diagnostic; video quality requires the existing real-model VBench/SSIM/PSNR pipeline.
